input.question: Why is it that we can remember some childhood memories so vividly, and others not at all?
input.ground_truth: From a psychological perspective we are more likely to remember memories that are associated with high emotion- usually negative emotion. So if you think of your earliest childhood memory it is usually a negative memory like being violently sick or getting in trouble.

Okay, let's imagine your brain is like a big toy box.

Some toys (which are your memories) are really special or fun, so you play with them a lot. That’s why you remember those memories very clearly—they got played with and remembered many times.

Other toys in the box you didn’t play with much, or maybe you played with them just once. So, it’s harder to find those toys later. That’s why some childhood memories are easy to remember and others you can’t find at all. Your brain keeps the toys you play with most!
